column15: Verified via Wikipedia (opened this session): Kentucky whiskey founded 1860, Brown-Forman owned it 1923-2020, sold to Sazerac Company mid-2020 alongside Canadian Mist. Domestically labeled "Kentucky Whisky" (some used-barrel-aged stock falls just short of the US bourbon standard) but marketed as bourbon internationally; kept defaultTypeName=bourbon as the catalogue's working category. No peat; bourbon.

Corrected from unresolved/unknown: real brand, "Easy Rider Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey," sourced and bottled by Hood River Distillers (Hood River, Oregon; official site opened), aged 4 years, motorcycle-culture branding tied to the 1969 film. Source distillery not disclosed. No peat mentioned.

Corrected from low/unresolved: real brand, a 12yo single grain Scotch finished in French Cognac/wine barriques, one of Brave New Spirits Ltd's volume brands (independent bottler, Glasgow, est. 2020 - IWSC listing opened confirms both). No peat mentioned (candied orange/oak notes). Source grain distillery undisclosed. Added brave-new-spirits as a new bottler row.

Corrected from low: Fitzwilliam is BBC Spirits' (French distributor) brand, distilled at Great Northern Distillery, Dundalk (both pages opened this session); range spans grain/malt/pot still/blended so defaultTypeName left empty. The Blended expression's own product page states "a touch of peat" / "a peat note towards the end of the palate" - the brand owner's own page, so peatProfile=light rather than unknown. GND separately sells a "Peated Single Malt" under this brand (see rule.tsv). Added great-northern-distillery as a new parent-distillery row.

Corrected from low: real brand, Flannigans Blended Irish Whiskey, produced by Irish Premium Spirits Company and bottled for Morrisons Supermarkets (UK), 40% ABV, soft citrus-led blend. No peat mentioned anywhere. (Whiskybase's own pages blocked direct fetch this session; corroborated by convergent independent search listings, incl. IWSC, agreeing on producer/bottler.)

Verified via Wikipedia (opened): Fuji Gotemba distillery, Shizuoka, established 1972 by Kirin Seagram, now Kirin Distillery Company; range spans Single Grain/Single Malt/Blended so defaultTypeName stays empty. Corrected peatProfile from none to unknown: nothing opened this session confirms the range is unpeated, and it should not be guessed. (The seed round's Kirin PDF would not render as text this session, so it is dropped as a citation; Wikipedia's distillery article is used instead.)

Corrected from low/unresolved: real brand, produced by Three Counties Spirits Ltd (Clonmel, Co. Tipperary), a triple-distilled grain-and-malt blend matured in ex-bourbon casks (sources vary on exact age/ratio). No peat mentioned. Named for the Irish folk ballad, as the seed note already said.

Corrected from unknown: real product, "Glant Bernard 3yo Blended Scotch Whisky," 40%, marketed by the Italian group Polini Distillates, Wines & Beverages for Eastern-European export (distilled/matured in Scotland per the opened product page). Honey/caramel/fruity profile, no peat. countryCode corrected from XX to GB-SCT - it is Scotch whisky; the Italian marketer is captured in owner instead.

Searched this session (plain name, plus the "No 3"/export angle); found only that it is listed for sale in 0.7L format on a Ukrainian retail aggregator, with no page that would open to give producer/bottler details. Left as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per the long-tail default; peatProfile=none is the category convention only, not brand evidence.

Corrected from low/unresolved: real range, "Glen Broch ... Single Malt Scotch Whisky" (10/12/25yo plus a Bourbon Cask Finish), bottled by Quality Spirits International - also behind Glengannon and Grangestone in this batch. IWSC's own listing (opened) states region=Speyside; a separate retailer had said Highland, but the structured IWSC data is preferred. No peat mentioned anywhere. kind kept as blend since the source distillery itself is undisclosed even though the product is single malt (see defaultTypeName).

Re-searched this session ("Glen Clan" plus Glen Turner/Bardinet); confirmed Glen Turner Company (part of La Martiniquaise-Bardinet, running Glen Moray + Starlaw and blends like Label 5/Sir Edward's/Glen Turner pure malt) is real, but no source names "Glen Clan" itself, so the brand's own identity stays unverified on the web - owner is kept from the project's first-party scrape evidence (alcomag/winebutik "Виробник" field) per be/CLAUDE.md, not a URL. See rule.tsv for the "Peated" expression named in the catalogue sample.

Confirmed as a real listed product, "Glen Russell Blended Scotch Whisky," 40%, 700ml, an own-label export blend; producer/bottler not named on any source found (Spirit Radar's own brand/distillery fields are blank on the opened page). No peat mentioned. Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per the long-tail default, now backed by a directly-opened confirming source.

column7: The Vintage Malt Whisky Co Ltd
column15: Corrected from low/own-label default: real brand, a blended malt from The Vintage Malt Whisky Co Ltd (est. 1992) marrying undisclosed Highland malts, named for the River Almond. No peat mentioned; described as mellow and honeyed. Added region/legalRegion=highland; corrected defaultTypeName from blend to malt (it is a blended malt, not a malt-and-grain blend).

Corrected from unknown/unresolved: real brand, launched in the 1960s by Rory MacDonald (Clachaig Inn, Glencoe), acquired by Ben Nevis Distillery in the early 1990s and now sold as Ben Nevis's in-house Blended Malt (parentSlug=ben-nevis; official product page opened). That page gives woody/nutty/orange-marmalade/chocolate notes with no peat mentioned at all. A retailer/blog separately described "a subtle touch of peat" in the 10yo - not the producer's own domain, so withheld. withheld peat proposal: light per divingforpearlsblog.com/tyndrumwhisky.com tasting notes.

Corrected from unknown/unresolved: real brand, "Glengannon Blended Malt Scotch Whisky" 5yo 40%, historically a pure-malt export brand of the Glengannon Whisky Company (an Invergordon Distillers subsidiary), now bottled by Quality Spirits International per IWSC's own listing (opened) - also behind Glen Broch/Grangestone in this batch. No peat mentioned anywhere. defaultTypeName corrected to malt (blended malt).

Confirmed on Het Anker's own site (opened): Belgian brewery (Mechelen) distilling single malt from its own Gouden Carolus Tripel mash since 2010, First Fill Bourbon casks then their own "Anker" casks; fruit/vanilla/creme-brulee profile, no peat. Het Anker also sells a separate "Gouden Carolus Single Malt Peated" line (see rule.tsv); this base/standard expression stays none.

Confirmed via canadianwhisky.org (opened): an inexpensive Canadian rye whisky blended in Canada, marketed mainly to Mexico; source distillery undisclosed (one secondary source names Alberta Distillers, another calls it undisclosed, so owner is left blank rather than guessed). No peat mentioned.

Corrected from low/"reportedly Aldi": not an Aldi own-label per anything found - it is Quality Spirits International's (a William Grant & Sons company) own branded range of affordable Highland single malts (Bourbon Cask/Rum Cask/Sherry Cask finishes), confirmed on QSI's own brand page (opened). No peat mentioned for any expression. Added region/legalRegion=highland; corrected defaultTypeName to single malt.

Corrected from unresolved/unknown: real brand, "Two James Grass Widow" - a sourced high-rye bourbon (36% rye/60% corn/4% barley) finished in ex-Madeira casks, bottled by Two James Spirits (Detroit, MI; official site opened). countryCode corrected from XX to US. No peat mentioned for this expression (Two James separately sells an unrelated "J. Riddle Peated Bourbon" under a different name).

Corrected countryCode from IE to US: the catalogued product is "Gravediggers Straight Bourbon Whiskey" (Category: Bourbon, Virgin Oak cask, 40%, bottled 2021 - page opened via browser), and "Straight Bourbon" is a protected US whiskey style, so the liquid is American even though its barcode carries an Irish (539-prefix) GS1 registration, which is presumably why the seed row read it as Irish. Bottler is listed only as "Distillery Bottling," source distillery undisclosed. No peat mentioned; standard bourbon.

Ownership freshly verified: historic Owensboro, KY distillery (founded 1885, revived 2016). Press coverage from 2022 says Bardstown Bourbon Company acquired Green River Distilling Co. that year, but the distillery's own site (opened today) credits itself "A Lofted Spirits Brand" rather than Bardstown directly - likely a later holding-company rename; both facts are noted rather than picking one blindly. "Green River Wheated" and the Kentucky Straight Bourbon range confirm defaultTypeName=bourbon. No peat mentioned.

Confidence raised from low to high: 20yo single grain selected by Stephanie Macleod, John Dewar & Sons' real Master Blender; homeofmalts.com (opened this session) explicitly categorizes it "non smoky," confirming peatProfile=none directly rather than only by category convention. Both retailer sources repeat that it is sourced from "Macduff," which is documented elsewhere as a malt-only distillery that cannot produce single grain whisky - kept unresolved/no parentSlug per the seed row's own caution, since this looks like a retailer copy error rather than a real Macduff connection.

Corrected from low/"not researched": real product, "Gwalarn Pure Malt" - a vatting of malt whiskies from Scotland, Germany and France, distinct from the base "Gwalarn" Celtic blend, made by Celtic Whisky Distillerie (Pleubian, Brittany; recently acquired by Maison Villevert, whose own site hosts this exact product page, opened this session). Their own description: "slightly peaty character" on the palate, "iodised and slightly smoky notes" - the brand owner's own domain, hence peatProfile=light. Sibling products from the same distillery, Kornog (heavily peated single malt) and Glann ar Mor (unpeated single malt), are not in this catalogue and were not added as rows. name corrected from "Gwalarn Pure" to the properly spelled "Gwalarn Pure Malt."

column7: Teeling family, Jim Finn & David Hynes
column15: new row for fitzwilliam. Dundalk, Co. Louth, on the former Harp Lager Brewery site; began distilling 2015; produces grain, pot still and single malt whiskey, both unpeated and peated - peatProfile left unknown since the range spans both.

new row for ecosse-g. Independent bottler and blender of Scotch whisky and rum, Glasgow, founded 2020; named Whisky Magazine's Independent Bottler of the Year and Spirits Business's 2024 Spirits Bottler of the Year. peatProfile=unknown per the bottler default.
